Our curriculum is registered with the New York State Education Department as meeting the 150-credit hour education requirements for licensure as a CPA. The program also provides an excellent foundation for students who wish to pursue graduate studies in accounting, business, or law.
Accredidation: The University at Buffalo School of Management is accredited by AACSB International - The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. [1]
QsWorldRanking: #1 Public university in New York State
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available.

[1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Architecture
Requirements: For automatic admission to the architecture major, first-year students must have a 3.0 minimum cumulative GPA for all coursework attempted. [2]
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Architecture is a pre-professional, four-year undergraduate degree that provides a solid foundation in the field of architecture. It is the first of two degrees required to become a licensed architect. The program combines a liberal arts education with a rigorous, studio-based curriculum that prepares students for graduate studies and a variety of career paths in design and the built environment. Students explore design, history, theory, technology, and representation, developing critical thinking and creative problem-solving skills.
ScholarshipAmount: Scholarships range from $1,000 to full tuition, with specific awards like the Provost's Scholars Award at $3,000 and the President's Scholars Award providing a full four-year scholarship. [13, 27]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art History

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art
Description: The Department of Art at the University at Buffalo prepares students for the real-world practice of visual art and scholarship. It unites the disciplines of fine art, design and emerging practices with art history and visual theory to equip students with an interdisciplinary approach to investigating and creating the visual world. Students have the opportunity to become proactive members of the arts community, gain professional experiences for their portfolio and resume, and build networks with faculty, staff, visiting artists, and peers.

You decide which Asian language (Arabic, Chinese, Hindi, Japanese, Korean) and which region of Asia most interests you, and then you develop your academic plan from there! You are required to take 4 semesters of an Asian language, and you can focus on history, language, culture, health, gender, popular culture or develop a broader understanding as you take your required upper level electives. [13]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biochemistry
Requirements: Applicants may apply to UB using the Common Application, Coalition Application, or the SUNY Application. [3] A $50 application fee is required with each option. [9] UB requires your high school transcript. [9] UB strongly recommends the submission of at least one letter of recommendation from a school counselor, teacher, community member or employer. [9] The University at Buffalo has adopted a test-optional policy, meaning standardized test scores are not needed for admission. [4]
Department: Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biological Sciences
Requirements: Admission to UB is based on a holistic review of each student. We consider both academic and non-academic factors, including your high school GPA and the overall strength of your academic coursework. We're looking to get a full picture of your accomplishments and potential, both in and out of the classroom.
Concentration: ['General Biological Sciences', 'Ecology, Evolution and Conservation Biology Concentration', 'Human Biology Concentration', 'Integrative Physiology and Neurobiology Concentration', 'Molecular, Cellular and Developmental Biology Concentration']
Description: The bachelor of science (BS) degree in biological sciences educates students broadly in biology. As a BS biological sciences student, you'll explore the structure, function, behavior and evolution of cells, organisms, populations and ecosystems. Students seeking a degree in biological sciences can opt for a general curriculum (BLS) or focus on a particular area by selecting one of our four concentrations. All these programs lead to a variety of overlapping postgraduation academic and career options; we encourage you to look at the differences in course requirements and select the curriculum that best matches your academic interests.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Engineering
Department: School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
Description: Biomedical engineers combine the problem solving ability of engineers with the knowledge of the biological and medical fields to develop new solutions for improving human health, healthcare, and quality of life for all people. The undergraduate program provides the scope of knowledge and training for employment in the field and also forms the basis for further study at the graduate level. [7] As an undergraduate student, you will learn to apply mathematical methods, science concepts, and experimental techniques of engineering to solve complex biological and medical problems in both the classroom and laboratory. [2] The undergraduate curriculum imparts fundamental learning in mathematics, physics, chemistry, basic biology, and engineering. [2] The Biomedical Engineering core courses provide you with a hands-on engineering experience that involves design and modeling. [2] The curriculum emphasizes four main areas (Imaging, Tissue Engineering, Sensor Materials and Devices, and Computation), and allows for students to obtain depth in areas of their choice through technical electives. [7]
Accredidation: The Biomedical Engineering BS program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET under the commission's General Criteria and Program Criteria for Bioengineering and Biomedical and Similarly Named Engineering Programs. [2, 3, 9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Sciences
Requirements: Application to the Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Sciences is through the general first-year undergraduate admissions process at the University at Buffalo. Applicants must submit a completed application, an official high school transcript, and at least one letter of recommendation. An essay is also a required part of the application.
Department: Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences
Description: The Biomedical Sciences major provides students with the knowledge and skills to be successful in a broad range of health-related fields, including medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, physician assistant, physical therapy, or any of the many other health sciences careers. [1] It provides a thorough foundation in biology's fundamental principles including organism function, cell biology, genetics, physiology and the research process. [1] Command of these core concepts is necessary for students to understand complex biological problems and to apply their knowledge to health-related problems. [1] Four health related natural science electives are required so that students can develop a strong understanding of the basis of human health. [1] Additionally, students must choose one course on societal perspectives on health which will expose them to a variety of health care concerns and provide a framework for the students to understand and have empathy for their patients. [1] The Biomedical Sciences major also emphasizes skills that students need to be effective health care providers. [1] The capstone experience focuses on clinical experiences that are necessary for students to gain perspective on the true nature of their chosen profession and required of all health-related graduate programs. [1] Students can utilize their health-related internships, study abroad, or research experience to apply what they have learned and satisfy the beyond the classroom learning requirement. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biotechnology
Requirements: While the State University of New York at Buffalo does not offer a specific major named 'Bachelor of Science in Biotechnology', it is available as a concentration within the Biological Sciences BA/BS program. General admission for undergraduate programs requires the submission of an application, a nonrefundable application fee, and academic transcripts. For first-year applicants, this includes a high school transcript. The university conducts a holistic review of applications, considering academic performance, the rigor of the curriculum, and other factors.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Biotechnology is an interdisciplinary program for students interested in scientific careers in the biotechnology industry. Students learn biotechnology theory and gain hands-on lab experience. The curriculum starts with foundational courses in biology and chemistry (like cell biology and organic chemistry) and moves to advanced subjects such as cell culture techniques, immunology, and genetics. Students create a personalized curriculum by choosing technical electives from various departments like anthropology, biology, chemistry, medicinal chemistry, biochemical pharmacology, and computer science to align with their career goals. [2, 15] Housed within the Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences, the program provides access to expert faculty and modern labs. [15]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration

[18] It prepares you to be effective and innovative in the workplace, and to undertake more advanced study. [18] The program is broadly based to prepare graduates for positions in engineering development, design, economic evaluation, sales, construction, production, and management. [2] Students will enhance their effectiveness at designing real world chemical processes as they enter the workplace. [2]
Accredidation: The Chemical Engineering BS program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET under the commission's General Criteria and Program Criteria for Chemical, Biochemical, Biomolecular, and Similarly Named Engineering Programs. [2, 3, 4, 8]

[3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering
Department: School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
Description: Students pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering (BSCE) may complete the degree with or without a concentration in Environmental Engineering. Within this degree, students may choose electives to permit additional exposure to selected areas of civil or environmental engineering design, such as transportation, structural, geotechnical, environmental and water resources engineering. In the environmental engineering concentration, electives may be selected to focus on water quality and treatment, bioremediation, solid and hazardous wastes, air quality and air pollution control. The undergraduate program gives students the theoretical background, instruction in engineering application of scientific principles and professional attitude to serve the public. It typically leads to entry-level positions or to graduate work in technical specialties (e.g., environmental, geotechnical, structural and transportation), business administration or other professions. a series of senior-level professional design courses. These simulate the design processes used in the major areas of civil engineering and prepare students for entry-level positions.
Accredidation: The Civil Engineering BS program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET under the commission's General Criteria and Program Criteria for Civil and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Classics
Concentration: ['Classical Languages and Literature', 'Classical Civilization', 'Greek and Roman Culture']
Description: The BA in Classics at the University at Buffalo allows undergraduate majors to explore the legacy of the Greek and Roman world and its historical significance in contemporary culture. [10] Students gain knowledge of the foundational elements of classics by studying the languages, history, art, archaeology, and culture of Greece and Rome. [10] The program develops students' ability to closely read and analyze texts, both in their original language and in translation. [10] This analytical skill is demonstrated through writing papers that draw on a variety of research tools, including texts, documents, physical artifacts, scholarly articles, theoretical approaches, and digital tools. [10] The Department of Classics at UB is the only one in the State University of New York (SUNY) system and provides a friendly, supportive program with numerous opportunities for research and travel. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Communication
Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering
Description: With the help of our constituents, we identify career objectives a computer engineer should be able to meet within a few years after graduation. We periodically survey our alumni and their employers to find out how well these objectives are being met. [1] We also survey and assess students throughout the duration of the BS program to determine if they are acquiring the skills and knowledge they will need to achieve the defined career objectives. [1] The program is outcomes-based—based on what our students know and can do, not based on what is covered in class—and devoted to continuous improvement. [1]
Accredidation: The BS degree in Computer Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
Description: The BS in Computer Science program is a comprehensive four-year curriculum that prepares students for a career in computer science. The program provides a thorough grounding in the fundamentals of computer science and is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET. Students in the program have the opportunity to explore a variety of advanced topics and engage in research with faculty. The curriculum is designed to provide a deep and broad understanding of computer science, covering areas from the mathematical and theoretical foundations to the practical aspects of software and hardware development.
Accredidation: The BS program in computer science is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Criminology
Description: As a criminology major, you'll ask tough questions about a topic that affects nearly every aspect of society, from health and housing to education and the environment. And then you'll learn where to find the clues to help answer them. Forget what you've seen on TV crime shows. Here, you'll take a critical, research-based look at criminology as you explore subjects such as: The relationship between crime, deviance and delinquency. Theories of crime. How we measure crime. Systems of power and how law contributes to inequality. Misconceptions and stereotypes. Disparities in the justice system related to race, ethnicity and gender. Experiences of incarcerated people. How behavior shapes policy (and vice versa). [15]

The third year involves coordinated sequences in electronics and electronic circuits, communications and signal processing, microprocessors and microcomputers, and electromagnetic theory. In the fourth year, students focus on reinforcing laboratory skills, practicing design, and broadening their knowledge through technical electives.

Description: The Engineering Physics BS program is intended for those students whose interests center on the more fundamental aspects of electrical engineering and physics, but who also wish to have extensive contact with the applied aspects (instrumentation, circuit design) of those subjects. The program is designed such that a student can pursue a graduate program in electrical engineering or applied physics, depending on their interest. This course of study provides students with a unique combination of the fundamental principles of modern electronics, as well as a thorough education in electrical measurements and instrumentation.
Accredidation: The Engineering Science BS program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET under the commission's General Criteria and Program Criteria for Engineering, General Engineering, Engineering Physics, Engineering Science, and Similarly Named Engineering Programs. ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Design
Description: This program is closely tied to some of the most complex problems facing society today, from climate change and community health to public safety and housing affordability. Students work in partnership with faculty to connect the art of design with how the world takes shape. Projects cultivate creative problem solving and develop skills that allow students to create places that are not only beautiful, but sustainable, healthy, and equitable.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering
Department: School of Engineering and Applied Sciences, Department of Civil, Structural and Environmental Engineering
Description: Environmental engineers work at the interface of society and the environment, striving to protect both human and ecosystem health. At UB, environmental engineers focus on sustainability, delivering safe drinking water and clean air, restoring the water quality of the Great Lakes, Hundson River and natural water systems everywhere and several other initiatives critical to environmental health.
Accredidation: Our undergraduate programs in civil engineering and environmental engineering are accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET and prepare students for graduate study and/or professional practice. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Geosciences
Description: Study the interactions between humans and the geologic environment that determine the habitability and sustainability of the planet, especially in relation to hydrology and water quality, soils, mineral resources, and climate change.

With a bachelor's degree, you will:Gain a solid knowledge base in various aspects of human physical activity—physiological, biomechanical and nutritional; Advance to graduate or professional study in the health sciences, including physical therapy, medicine, chiropractic or physician assistant programs; Succeed in your career in settings such as hospitals, educational institutions, corporations, fitness facilities and community centers.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Film Studies
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Film Studies offers students in-depth education in the disciplinary understanding of film as an aesthetic medium and in the critical analysis of films as cultural objects laden with ideological, racial, and gendered meanings. [3] Students will gain an understanding of aspects of cinematic aesthetics, film grammar, the history of film, cultural contexts of film, and theoretical and critical approaches in film studies. [3] The Film Studies Program, housed in the Office of Interdisciplinary Studies, is an interdisciplinary program with courses in the departments of Africana Studies, American Studies, Art, Communications, English, History, Languages, Cultures and Translation, Political Science, Religious Studies, Theatre, and Women's and Gender Studies. [1] The Program teaches film as an art form; a conduit of popular culture; a community-building tool; and agent of change. [1]

The Global Gender Studies undergraduate program offers courses in three areas: Cultures and Identities; Women and Global Citizenship; and Gender and Public Policy. Our courses synthesize local and global knowledge, linking gender to history, literature and policy. Throughout their course of study, students will benefit from the expertise of professors preparing them for graduate work and employment in a wide range of fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Geography
Concentration: ['General Geography', 'Earth Systems Science', 'Urban and Regional Analysis']
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Geography at the University at Buffalo allows students to think critically about the location and spatial arrangement of human and natural phenomena and their contribution to various environmental and societal issues. The program is flexible, with a few required courses and a wide selection of electives in areas such as earth science, urban geography, development geography, forest ecology, environmental hazards, health behaviors, oceans, and international trade. Students learn to collect, describe, analyze, and interpret data, as well as create and analyze maps and models. They also receive hands-on training in relevant software for their future careers. [2, 7]

[4] As a geological sciences student, you'll typically take classes in chemistry, calculus and physics, as well as geology and related subjects. [4] Of course, you'll also have hands-on labs where you can study specimens up close and learn how to use specialized tools. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in German
Description: Spoken by more than 100 million people in Germany, Austria, Switzerland and throughout the world, German is a major international language of business, diplomacy, science, and popular culture. Germany's economy is the largest in the European Union, and the sixth largest in the world. German is a key language in the fields of music, psychology, philosophy, theology, and the natural sciences. The German BA is designed for students who want to be fluent in German, study one of the largest economies in the European Union, and learn more about the birthplace of Einstein, Arendt, Nietzsche, Beethoven and other world-famous Germans. Our graduates have used their language skills to work in business, education, government and the non-profit sector. German classes are typically small in size, allowing for greater interaction, face-time and use of the target language between the instructor and students. Courses cover a variety of topics, and Independent Studies may be arranged to suit a student's particular goals.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Global Affairs
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Global Affairs equips students to tackle critical questions about global systems, international politics and global economics. This interdisciplinary program delves into international law, global policies, human rights and conflict resolution, preparing students to understand and influence an interconnected world. Whether you're interested in international relations, global governance, or human rights advocacy, this program provides the tools to make an impact. Graduates find rewarding careers in non-governmental organizations (NGOs), international organizations, government service, and beyond.
